title: Electrode potentials: predicting the voltage

concepts.label: cell voltages add up
concepts.definition: A voltage (in volts, read by a voltmeter) belongs to a pair of half-cells, and the voltages of pairs chain like height differences: Zn–Cu 1.10 V + Cu–Ag 0.46 V = Zn–Ag 1.56 V.

concepts.label: electrode potential
concepts.definition: One number per half-cell such that a cell's voltage is the difference of two of them; only differences are measurable, so the zero is a convention.

concepts.label: standard hydrogen electrode (SHE)
concepts.definition: The agreed zero of the potential scale: platinum in 1 mol/L H⁺ with H₂ gas at 1 bar, 2H⁺ + 2e⁻ ⇌ H₂, defined as exactly 0 V.

concepts.label: standard conditions
concepts.definition: Every dissolved species at 1 mol/L, every gas at 1 bar, pure solids and liquids, tables quoted at 25 °C; marked by the ° sign.

concepts.label: standard reduction potential E°
concepts.definition: The potential of a half-cell against the SHE under standard conditions, with the half-reaction written as a reduction (ox + n e⁻ → red); more positive means the oxidised form pulls electrons harder.

concepts.label: electrochemical series (potential ladder)
concepts.definition: The table of half-reactions sorted by E°, drawn as a ladder with the most negative E° (strongest electron-givers) at the top so that electrons fall downwards; it is the activity series with numbers.

concepts.label: E°cell = E°cathode − E°anode
concepts.definition: The standard voltage of a cell is the reduction potential of the cathode half-cell minus that of the anode half-cell, both taken unchanged from the table.

concepts.label: positive E°cell = spontaneous
concepts.definition: If E°cell is positive the reaction runs by itself in the direction written (galvanic cell); if negative, the reverse reaction is the spontaneous one.

concepts.label: E° is per electron (never multiplied)
concepts.definition: A potential is a push per electron (a height, not an amount), so multiplying a half-reaction to balance electrons leaves its E° unchanged.

concepts.label: strongest oxidising / reducing agents
concepts.definition: Reduced forms at the negative end of the ladder are the strongest reducing agents (Li, −3.04 V) and oxidised forms at the positive end the strongest oxidising agents (F₂, +2.87 V); a reducing agent reacts spontaneously with any oxidising agent on a lower rung.

summary: Running example: the Daniell cell (1.10 V) with iron and silver half-cells as companions; measured pair voltages chain like heights, which leads to one potential per half-cell, the hydrogen zero, standard conditions and E°. The table (Chem.E0) is drawn throughout as a ladder with the most negative E° at the top so electrons fall downwards; E°cell = E°cathode − E°anode is the drop, positive = spontaneous, and E° is never multiplied by coefficients (Zn + 2Ag⁺, 1.56 V). Capstone: a cell builder over all Chem.E0 half-cells giving voltage, anode/cathode, electron direction and the balanced overall reaction, with presets later lessons can refer back to (H₂/O₂ 1.23 V, Pb/PbO₂ 2.05 V, Cd/NiO(OH) 1.30 V, Li/F₂ 5.91 V).
